title: Good news for the northern districts
full_text:
The city council has announced that it will extend the tram line to the northern districts. We welcome this decision because a fast tram connection means fewer cars on our streets and cleaner air for everyone.

For years we collected signatures and wrote to every council member. Today we are proud, because our persistence has paid off and we look forward to the first construction works next spring.

Join our volunteers on Saturday at the main square, where we will celebrate the council decision with music and free coffee.

title: Repair cafe number three opens
full_text:
Our volunteers organise a repair cafe in the old library, where neighbours bring broken toasters, bicycles and lamps. More than sixty people came on the first evening and almost every device left working again.

We believe that repairing things is a small but real answer to the climate crisis. Every repaired device saves resources, and the evening brings people together who would never meet otherwise.

title: October newsletter
full_text:
The city council has opened a public consultation on the plan to extend the tram line. We encourage everyone to take part, because a strong response will show the council that residents want the tram line extended.

We are optimistic that the extension will be built on time, since the council has promised funding in the next budget.

Our work depends on small donations. Support the collective with a monthly gift of 5 euros and help us keep our campaigns independent and free of corporate money.

title: Solar panels for our schools
full_text:
An energy cooperative has started to install solar panels on the roofs of three schools in the district. Pupils can follow the electricity production on a screen in the entrance hall, and the schools will save thousands of euros a year.

We support this project fully and call on the council to open more public roofs for citizen energy projects.

title: Council postpones the tram decision
full_text:
The city council has postponed its final decision on the tram line extension to the northern districts. The council says that more studies are needed, but we are unsure whether this is a real reason or just a delay.

We still hope that the extension will come, yet we are no longer certain. We will watch the next council session closely and report what we see.

title: December newsletter
full_text:
Our volunteers organise repair cafes in three districts now, and the fourth one will open in January. Hundreds of devices were saved from the bin this autumn and the volunteers are proud of what they have built together.

Please bring tools and spare parts if you have some, and tell your neighbours about the repair cafes.

title: Speech at the winter rally
full_text:
The city council has cut the budget for the tram line extension to the northern districts. After years of promises, the council now takes the money away, and we are furious about this broken promise.

Cars will continue to clog the northern districts, and the people who live there pay the price with their health. The council chooses the motorway lobby over its own citizens, and we will not accept that.

We demand that the council restores the tram line extension in the budget immediately.

title: The tram line is delayed again
full_text:
The city council has delayed the tram line extension again, this time without any new date. This is outrageous, because the council promised the extension in writing and now ignores its own decision.

Residents of the northern districts wait for a connection that never arrives. We accuse the council of failing a whole generation of commuters and young people who depend on public transport.

title: Tool library joins the repair cafes
full_text:
Our volunteers now run a tool library next to the repair cafes, where neighbours can borrow drills, ladders and sewing machines for free. Sharing tools instead of buying them cuts waste and costs.

The tool library shows that neighbourhood projects work when volunteers take responsibility, even when the council does not act.

title: March newsletter
full_text:
The city council has cancelled the tram line extension to the northern districts. We feel that nothing we do can change the council and many of us are tired and discouraged after years of campaigning.

Some volunteers ask whether it still makes sense to write letters to a council that does not listen.

title: Rooftop solar reaches a fourth school
full_text:
The energy cooperative has finished the solar installation on a fourth school roof. Together the panels now cover the yearly electricity use of two hundred households.

We celebrate this success and invite other neighbourhoods to start their own citizen energy projects.

title: We will not give up on the tram
full_text:
We refuse to accept the cancellation of the tram line extension to the northern districts. Our volunteers launch a new campaign to force the city council to reinstate the extension, and we will collect twenty thousand signatures.

The council may have cancelled the tram line, but it cannot cancel our resolve. We will march through the northern districts every month until the council restores the extension.

title: May newsletter
full_text:
More than twelve thousand people have signed our petition so far, and the repair cafes keep growing. Volunteers organise repair cafes and a tool library in four districts and new helpers join every week.

Come to our next planning evening and bring a friend.

title: Speech in front of the council building
full_text:
The city council has reinstated the tram line extension to the northern districts after months of pressure from residents. We are overjoyed, because this victory shows that persistent citizens can change a council decision.

We will keep watching the council, but today we celebrate. The extension will be built, and the northern districts will finally get their tram connection.

title: June newsletter
full_text:
The tram line extension to the northern districts is back in the council budget and the first construction date has been announced. We thank every volunteer who signed, marched and wrote letters.

Summer repair cafes start next week, so please check our website for the dates.
